To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
certain nucleotides in a complex of the M1 RNA, an RNA enzyme, with tRNA precursor molecule are protected from chemical modifications that occur in the absence of substrate.

the pattern of protection is similar in M1 RNA and 23S rDNA, that the substrate is not folded when it is in the ES complex, and that the substrate is unfolded when it is in a complex with the RNA subunit of the enzyme.

the nucleotide sequence of M1 RNA is not important for catalysis, that the catalytic RNA can form complexes with tRNA precursors that resemble the Michaelis complex, and that the substrate in this complex is in a partially unfolded conformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structure-function relationship of the ribozyme RNase P.
the mechanism of RNA catalysis.
the mechanism of RNA catalyzed reactions and how RNA enzymes interact with their substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RNA enzyme and the tRNA precursor molecule form a Michaelis complex in which the substrate is in a conformation that is similar to the E site of ribosomes.
chemical modification studies have shown that the ES complex has a structure similar to that of the E site and that the substrate is not in an unfolded con formation in the complex.
the pattern of protection is similar in both cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RNA enzyme and its substrate interact in a way similar to the interaction of 23S rRNAs with tRNA.

we have found that the M1 RNA is protected from chemical modification of certain nucleotides when M1 RNA is complexed with tRNA precursors, and that the pattern of protection is similar to that of the E site.
the substrate is bound to the RNA enzyme in an open conformation, with the substrate's anticodon stem-loop in a position to be cleaved by the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RNA enzyme can bind to a tRNA precursor and that the binding of a tRNA precursor induces conformational changes in M1 RNA and in the tRNA precursor.
the RNA enzyme can bind and process its substrates without the help of proteins.
M1 RNA and the substrate tRNA precursor are in a conformation that is different from the one they adopt during the enzymatic reaction.
